summary.name: Tropy
summary.one_liner: Tropy is free, open-source software for organizing, describing, and annotating photographs of archival research material.
use_cases: Transcribing handwritten or printed documents from photos
Exporting research data to Omeka S
Tagging and listing research items for a writing project
summary.what_it_does: Tropy turns research photographs into items that can be described with customizable templates capturing the user's own subject knowledge. Users can organize items with tags and lists rather than following the structure of a physical archive. The annotation tools allow transcribing documents, selecting image details, and manipulating photos for clearer viewing. Research projects can be exported as JSON-LD, CSV, or directly to Omeka S, and custom export plugins can be created. Data is stored in SQLite.
notable: Stores research data in SQLite, which the page says the Library of Congress recommends for preservation
Exports to JSON-LD, CSV, and directly to Omeka S
Extensible via custom export plugins and core plugins
Developed by RRCHNM, C²DH, and Digital Scholar, funded by the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation
caveats: Page does not specify platform-specific limitations or version details beyond the listed operating systems
